driver_archetypes.rationale: Compliant car baseline. High tau (2.5s) ensures cars stop at red (M2/early/car ~0). Params unchanged to maintain discharge headway (M1/car).
Car violators (custom2) drawing from 'car' distribution. Params identical to car_saval to maintain low red-running and early-start behavior.
Compliant motorcycle baseline. Reduced share (0.6) allows 'moto_seeker' to capture the observed wrong-lane and early-start metrics while keeping overall density near observation (M5/moto_density).

Motorcycle violators drawing from 'moto' distribution. Increased share (0.4) boosts the probability of triggering `queue_space_seeking` to match observed wrong-lane shares (M8/moto ~0.21). Identical physical params to moto_saval.

Illegal left-turning motorcycles (distribution moto_violator). Share 1.0 ensures the 'moto_violator' distribution sums to exactly 1.0. jmTimegapMinor=1.0s controls box-waiting duration for illegal left turns.

traci_rules.rationale: Reduced base probability p0/p_max from 0.5 to 0.2. The previous high value caused excessive red-running (M3/share/moto ~0.09) and overshoot (M4/overshoot_share). Lowering this allows the `early_start` rule to dominate the red-running count, matching observations better.

Targets M2/early/moto (observed share 0.1303). Increasing p from the low values in prev iteration to 0.16 compensates for the lower share of `moto_seeker` and aims to reach the weighted observed mean. This also contributes significantly to M3/share/moto and M4/overshoot_share.

Targets M8/moto wrong-lane share (obs 0.2131). Since 'moto_seeker' has a share of 0.4 in total motorcycle demand, setting p_wrong_lane=0.55 yields an effective usage probability of roughly 0.22 per total motorcycle (0.4 * 0.55 ≈ 0.22), matching the observation. q=30m is the lower bound to trigger seeking early.
Field observation: most motorcycles pass a standing U-turner; p=0.8 (80% probability) and t_wait=2s reflects quick lateral filtering.
Field observation: cars rarely bypass standing U-turners; p=0.1 (10% probability) matches conservative car behaviour.
